Hi Alex / Elena  thanks for the questions. Below are concise answers and recommended configurations based on your e-discovery and compliance needs. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you'd like to walk through with logs examples.

SOC 2 / HIPAA / GDPR
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (Security + Confidentiality) on 2026-11-02. We can share the report under NDA  please tell us where to upload.
- HIPAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workloads on Dedicated and Private deployments and offers a BAA. Hosted (shared) is evaluated case-by-case; we can discuss details with legal.
- GDPR: We support regional deployments and customer-controlled data residency for Dedicated / Private. For hosted, PII controls and data processing addendum are available; we will provide the standard DPA.

Audit logging specifics
- What we capture:
  * Admin activity logs: console and control-plane actions (user invites, role changes, model rollouts, config changes), IP, actor, timestamp, affected resources, before/after values where applicable.
  * API logs: request metadata (method, endpoint, timestamp, latency, status code), request and response headers, and request payloads if customer enables full-request logging. By default, hosted accounts redact sensitive fields and do not persist full model inputs for >30 days unless explicitly enabled (opt-in).

- Request/response payloads and redaction:
  * Default (hosted): we persist metadata and request/response headers; payloads are truncated/redacted by default for PII-sensitive fields.
  * Dedicated / Private: customers can enable full-request capture and control retention/rotation. We provide tooling to mask/redact fields prior to storage if required.

Retention & immutability
- Hosted defaults: API logs retained 90 days; admin activity logs retained 365 days.
- Dedicated: configurable retention up to multi-year; recommended for e-discovery is 7 years if required.
- Immutability: we support WORM semantics via S3 Object Lock for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers, we can provide export snapshots and/or set up write-once export to your S3 with Object Lock enabled on your side.

Export / streaming options
- Near-real-time streaming: Kinesis, Pub/Sub, or HTTP endpoint to push events to Splunk/Datadog/SIEM.
- Batch exports: daily JSON/CSV dumps to a customer S3 bucket (encrypted).
- On-demand: Console CSV/JSON export for selected time ranges.

Formats & fields
- Exports available as newline-delimited JSON (recommended) or CSV. Each event includes: event_id, timestamp, actor, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, http_method, endpoint, status_code, latency_ms, request_size_bytes, response_size_bytes, and custom metadata tags.

Recommended next steps
1) Please upload the vendor_security_questionnaire_acme.pdf to our secure upload link (https://redwood-internal.s3/secure-upload/acme/questionnaire)  we'll track in HubSpot.
2) Tell us which deployment you expect (Hosted vs Dedicated). If Dedicated, we'll propose a retention/immutability plan and a sample S3 Object Lock configuration.
3) If you want example logs, we can produce a 1-day anonymized sample (JSON) demonstrating fields.

Attachments: Technical note (redwood-audit-logs-overview.pdf)  same doc Marissa attached.

Let me know if you'd like a call  happy to present examples.
